content:
maria: Heads-up — noticed the console sparklines + heatmap pages hang for ~2-3s on initial load after today's telemetry-client bump. Can reproduce on canary and a local prod-build. Screenshot: https://img.redwood.example/heatmap-freeze.png
kevin: ugh. saw one perf alert earlier but assumed telemetry sampling noise. any stack traces or flamegraphs?
sam: I grabbed a CPU profile from canary: main thread spikes around module evaluation, lots of time in `TelemetryClient.init` and `telemetry/shared/index.js` parse path.
sophie: that sounds like the new telemetry index bundle pulled in legacy utils — maybe an accidental commonjs -> esbuild duplication.
maria: here's the minimal repro we used locally:
```
// main-dashboard.tsx
import { initTelemetry } from 'telemetry/shared';
// later on mount
initTelemetry({ sampling: 0.01 });
```
When we lazy-load the charts the telemetry import still runs synchronously during hydration.
kevin: can we confirm chunking? `npx source-map-explorer` on the canary build shows `telemetry/shared` duplicated across 3 chunks: main, charts, heatmap. That duplication explains extra eval time and memory churn.
sam: also noticed KV cache misses spike at the same time (kvcache miss % + top-level import evaluation). Might be GC pressure from the duplicated bundles.
maria: deploy-bot shows the telemetry bump merged in PR 6721 (author: analytics/telemetry-team).
deploy-bot: deploy finished: canary-2026-03-20T09:12Z (commit 9f2a3b) :rocket:
kevin: quick mitigation options: 1) revert the telemetry bump; 2) change import to dynamic `await import('telemetry/shared')` inside a `useEffect`; 3) ensure telemetry is single-module via alias/rollup config so tree-shaking works.
sophie: option 2 is fastest short-term for charts that are slow because telemetry doesn't need to init during SSR/hydration. We should be careful with events that must fire during cold-start though.
maria: +1 for dynamic import in chart entrypoints as a quick canary patch. I'll open a tiny PR to change to `onMount` dynamic import and gate init by `if (typeof window !== 'undefined')`.
sam: can we also add a tiny canary metric: track main-thread evaluation time at startup and kvcache miss rate so we can detect if the fix helps? I can add a short-lived telemetry counter.
kevin: add a dashboard widget for that metric in the canary org so PMs can eyeball it. Sophie, can you coordinate?
sophie: on it. I'll also ping telemetry-team to do a follow-up to dedupe exports and check the bundler config. @analytics-team can we get a quick look?
maria: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-console/pull/7744 — patch changes import to dynamic in chart mount. Running local prod-build looks promising (no 2-3s freeze in my profile).
deploy-bot: canary deploy queued: patch/7744 -> canary
kevin: if the canary looks good for an hour with load-tests, let's roll to prod. Also assign an owner to follow the telemetry bundling cleanup so we don't regress.
sam: running a k6 script now against canary to simulate heavy dashboard load, will post numbers in 20m.
maria: thanks everyone. TL;DR: root cause = telemetry-client import getting duplicated into multiple chunks causing sync eval and main-thread stalls; short-term fix = dynamic import on chart mount; follow-up = dedupe telemetry bundle at build. :thumbsup:
